chapter: Later tours, illness and the union job
title: The Sir Charles Thompson and Witherspoon fight in Geneva
summary: On the 1961 tour, rivalry between Thompson and Witherspoon led to a brawl in an after-hours club, with Emmett Berry hitting Spoon with a trumpet.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Well, the band was about the same but the behavior was different. The behavior of the guys, especially towards the last,

they were, some of them were going to fight you know. They did have a big fight in Geneva, right on the band stand. But it wasn't at work, it was in an after-hours place. And the crowds, all of them had left the concert to go to this place because they knew we were going to play, going there anyway. And there's always been a rivalry between Sir Charles and Jimmy Witherspoon, something that happened out in California.

And anyway, that's where it started. The people, we had been playing. Somebody announced Jimmy Witherspoon and he said, okay, I'll sing. He got up and sang and it went down nice, people clapped, applauded. Now Sir Charles didn't like that because he got the applause. He hated that.

So without waiting for Witherspoon to decide what he was going to sing next, he went into da da, da da, da dum, which is a band number. sings From the Jam Blues' So we had to, we all went in and joined and we cut Witherspoon out. (LAUGHTER).
Well when it was over Jimmy Witherspoon stepped off the band stand and Sir Charles was standing in the way. He says, get out of the way.

So and so and so on. So Sir Charles says, go around me, so and so and so forth. Well then they, it's beginning to cussing and fighting and from somewhere Emmett Berry reached over with his trumpet and hit Spoon right on the head.

Oh, and there's Spoon laying down on the floor. He says, 'you hit me!' And Emmett Berry says, 'let that be a lesson to you. Don't you never fool with musicians.' (LAUGHTER). Because he was a singer. He took up for Sir Charles because he was a musician and Jimmy Witherspoon was a singer.
Oh boy, then I had, I was playing 'Body and Soul' and Gene Ramey trying to play a bass solo and I'm holding Spoon with one hand and Emmett Berry with the other hand.
Oh Gene Ramey is playing solo.

He's playing 'Body and Soul' and I'm trying to hold these two guys from fighting. So the guy comes up and says, Mr. Clayton they are going to call the police if you don't do something. So I made them get off the stand. As soon as they got back in the back they took off their coats and were going to fight. So I told them I says, well I

had to lecture. So I said, now the only thing you can do is to go on out there and act like you brothers, just had a fight in the family. So I made them shake hands and they went on out and finished the night without Sir Charles because he had gone on home.
